coverage.headline: Senate Seeks Expanded Sub V; Harvest Sherwood Plan OK'd
coverage.summary: Law360's weekly mid-cap roundup noted that food distributor Harvest Sherwood confirmed its Chapter 11 plan, alongside other major bankruptcy developments including TPx Communications' new postpetition financing. The plan confirmation marks a key milestone for unsecured creditors awaiting recoveries from antitrust litigation proceeds.

coverage.headline: Senate Seeks Expanded Sub V; Harvest Sherwood Plan OK'd
coverage.summary: Law360 reported that food distributor Harvest Sherwood confirmed its Chapter 11 plan, noting the confirmation as a key milestone alongside other bankruptcy developments that week.

coverage.headline: Senate Seeks Expanded Sub V; Harvest Sherwood Plan OK'd
coverage.summary: Law360's weekly wrap-up confirms Harvest Sherwood's Chapter 11 plan confirmation, noting the plan funder Atlas Grove will pursue over $1 billion in antitrust claims against meat producers as the primary vehicle for creditor recoveries.

coverage.headline: Harvest Sherwood Wins Ch. 11 Plan Approval
coverage.summary: Defunct food distributor Harvest Sherwood received confirmation of its Chapter 11 plan at a hearing on Wednesday after a Texas bankruptcy judge overruled a remaining objection from the U.S. Trustee's Office. The confirmation clears the way for the estate to pursue over $1 billion in antitrust litigation claims via Atlas Grove as plan funder.

coverage.headline: Harvest Sherwood Wins Ch. 11 Plan Approval
coverage.summary: A Texas bankruptcy judge confirmed Harvest Sherwood Food Distributors' Chapter 11 liquidation plan, overruling a remaining objection from the U.S. Trustee's Office. The plan centers on monetizing more than $1 billion in antitrust litigation claims for the benefit of creditors.

coverage.headline: U.S. Trustee Objects to Plan Confirmation Over Opt-Out Third-Party Releases and Proposed Charitable Donation of Residual Trust Funds
coverage.summary: The U.S. Trustee filed an objection asking the court to deny confirmation of Harvest Sherwood's Third Amended Plan, targeting opt-out third-party release provisions and a proposed charitable donation of residual trust funds, ahead of the August 5 confirmation hearing.

coverage.headline: Atlas Grove Gains Court Approval for $180MM Financing Commitment for Harvest Sherwood Bankruptcy Estate
coverage.summary: Atlas Grove Management received court approval and funded a $150 million DIP facility to the Harvest Sherwood bankruptcy estate and is acting as stalking-horse bidder for the exit funding process. As plan funder, Atlas Grove would seek to maximize value from over $1 billion in antitrust litigation claims against more than 25 defendants.

coverage.headline: Atlas Grove Announces Court Approval of $180 Million Financing Commitment for Harvest Sherwood Bankruptcy Estate
coverage.summary: Atlas Grove Management announced court approval of a $150 million DIP facility to the Harvest Sherwood estate and confirmed its role as stalking-horse exit funder; as plan funder, Atlas Grove aims to maximize value from more than $1 billion in antitrust litigation claims against 25+ defendants in chicken, pork, and beef markets.

coverage.headline: Atlas Grove Announces Court Approval of $180 Million Financing Commitment for Harvest Sherwood Bankruptcy Estate
coverage.summary: Atlas Grove Management announced court approval of a $150 million DIP facility to the Harvest Sherwood estate and its selection as stalking-horse plan funder, with the exit financing confirmation hearing slated for August 2026. As plan funder, Atlas Grove aims to maximize value from more than $1 billion in antitrust claims against 25+ defendants across chicken, pork, and beef industries.

coverage.headline: Court Opinion Review: A Joyous Mess in Harvest Sherwood
coverage.summary: Octus/Reorg reviewed the procedural history of the Harvest Sherwood case, covering early DIP disputes with the U.S. Trustee, Sprouts Farmers Market, and Burford Capital over the $1 billion-plus antitrust litigation proceeds and the court's rulings on venue and DIP approval.

coverage.headline: Harvest Sherwood Gets OK On $150M Replacement DIP
coverage.summary: A Texas bankruptcy judge approved Harvest Sherwood's $150 million replacement DIP financing facility and set bidding procedures for its exit funding, overcoming an objection from a litigation party. The court also approved bidding procedures for the exit-financing process.

coverage.headline: Harvest Sherwood Gets OK On $150M Replacement DIP
coverage.summary: A Texas bankruptcy judge approved Harvest Sherwood's $150 million replacement Chapter 11 DIP financing from Atlas Grove and set bidding procedures for exit funding, overcoming an objection from a litigation finance firm.

coverage.headline: Harvest Sherwood Gets OK On $150M Replacement DIP
coverage.summary: A Texas bankruptcy judge approved Harvest Sherwood's $150 million replacement DIP financing from Atlas Grove Management and set bidding procedures for its exit funding, defeating a litigation funder's objection. Atlas Grove, the stalking-horse plan funder, is positioned to oversee recovery of the estate's $1 billion-plus antitrust claims.

coverage.headline: Creditor Vote Set For Harvest Sherwood Liquidation Plan
coverage.summary: Harvest Sherwood received court clearance for an August confirmation hearing for its Chapter 11 liquidation plan after the Texas bankruptcy judge found the plan disclosure statement, with some tweaks, contained sufficient information for creditors.

coverage.headline: Creditor Vote Set For Harvest Sherwood Liquidation Plan
coverage.summary: Harvest Sherwood received court clearance to solicit creditor votes on its Chapter 11 liquidation plan, with a Texas bankruptcy judge approving the disclosure statement subject to certain tweaks and scheduling an August confirmation hearing. The plan centers on distributing proceeds from ongoing antitrust and Sprouts litigation through a post-confirmation trust.

coverage.headline: Creditor Vote Set For Harvest Sherwood Liquidation Plan
coverage.summary: Harvest Sherwood Food Distributors received court clearance for an August confirmation hearing for its Chapter 11 liquidation plan after a Texas bankruptcy judge found the plan disclosure statement, with some tweaks, contained sufficient information on what creditors can expect to receive. The plan relies on recoveries from over $1 billion in antitrust litigation claims against meat producers.
